items.stem: A queueing simulation keeps a reservoir of k = 5 customer records with Algorithm R, numbering records from 1. Customer 40 arrives. What is the probability that customer 40 is written into slot 3 at that moment? Give a decimal.

A particle-detector simulation emits collision events one at a time. You do not know how many events the run will produce, and you can store only 100. Which scheme gives every event the same probability of being among the 100 stored at the end of the run?

options.text: Store the first 100 events and ignore every event after them
Accept event i with probability 100/i and overwrite the oldest stored event
Accept each event with probability 1/2 and overwrite a random stored event
Accept event i with probability 100/i and overwrite a random stored event
Accept each event with probability 100/N, N being the run length planned beforehand
Store every 1000th event and drop the oldest stored event when storage is full

items.stem: Algorithm R runs with k = 3 over a stream that turns out to have n = 12 records. Record 4 has just been written into the reservoir. Given that, what is the probability that record 4 is still in the reservoir after record 12? Give a decimal to three places.

A classmate claims Algorithm R favors early records: the first k records enter the reservoir with certainty, while record i > k enters only with probability k/i. In one or two sentences, explain why every record still ends in the final sample with the same probability, and state that probability for a stream of n records.

A traffic simulation produces n = 1000 vehicle records, and Algorithm R keeps k = 10 of them. Record 7 goes into the reservoir as soon as it arrives. What is the probability that record 7 is in the reservoir at the end of the run?

A ray tracer streams four candidate lights for one pixel through a one-item weighted reservoir (add w to a running sum w_sum, then replace the stored light with probability w / w_sum). The weights arrive in the order 4, 1, 3, 2. What is the probability that the third light (weight 3) is the final stored light? Give a decimal.

In a renderer's one-item light reservoir, a programmer changes the update so a new candidate light replaces the stored one only when its weight is larger than the stored light's weight. Over many frames, which lights for a pixel ever get chosen, and what goes wrong in the rendered image? Answer in one or two sentences.

Three candidate lights stream through a one-item weighted reservoir (add w to w_sum, then replace with probability w / w_sum) with weights 2, 6 and 4, in that order. After the second candidate, the stored light is the second one (weight 6). Given that, what is the probability it is still the stored light after the third candidate? Give a decimal to three places.
